chapters.title: Should Have Been a Statistic
chapters.sourcePressure: A violent childhood in Buffalo, forced night work at the family skating rink, escape to Brazil, Indiana, and the refusal to let real damage become destiny.
chapters.coreMove: Separate what happened to you from the authority it still claims over your next move.
chapters.commonMisread: A generic resilience origin story where hardship automatically makes someone stronger.

chapters.title: Truth Hurts
chapters.sourcePressure: Wilmoth Irving's murder, racist hostility, academic failure, a failed Air Force test, and the Accountability Mirror as harsh truth plus daily work.
chapters.coreMove: Turn the private ugly fact into a posted task before shame can hide it again.

chapters.title: The Impossible Task
chapters.sourcePressure: An overweight exterminator sees the SEAL target and accepts a brutal weight-loss deadline that turns disgust into a fully priced mission.
chapters.coreMove: Replace a vague wish with a mission whose deadline and cost force daily behavior to change.
chapters.commonMisread: Extreme goals are inspiring because they are big.

chapters.title: Taking Souls
chapters.sourcePressure: BUD/S and Hell Week expose him to institutional pressure, group strain, and the tactic of using relentless effort to break the other side's morale first.
chapters.coreMove: Use visible refusal to quit to change the pressure in a shared ordeal.
chapters.commonMisread: Intimidate people or act cruel to prove toughness.

chapters.title: Armored Mind
chapters.sourcePressure: Repeated injury, insecurity, humiliation, and return during the SEAL pipeline make mental armor a practiced response, not invincibility.
chapters.coreMove: Treat a setback as a return drill instead of proof that the armor failed.

chapters.title: It's Not About a Trophy
chapters.sourcePressure: The San Diego 100 becomes a brutal test of motive, service to fallen servicemen's families, bodily toll, and the cookie jar as stored proof.
chapters.coreMove: Use a duty larger than winning to keep moving when the body starts asking for a smaller reason.
chapters.commonMisread: Endurance matters because medals prove character.

chapters.title: The Most Powerful Weapon
chapters.sourcePressure: Endurance work after San Diego frames the 40% rule, the protective governor, and the need to test limits with planning rather than reckless denial.
chapters.coreMove: Interrogate the first stop signal as a negotiation, then test it with pacing and judgment.
chapters.commonMisread: Ignore every limit because the body is lying.

chapters.title: Talent Not Required
chapters.sourcePressure: Larger endurance efforts reveal that grit without planning wastes capacity, and underperformance becomes a lesson in execution quality.
chapters.coreMove: Keep the engine, but fix the route, fuel, timing, and tactics before trying harder.
chapters.commonMisread: Talent is irrelevant, so strategy is optional.

chapters.title: Uncommon Amongst Uncommon
chapters.sourcePressure: Ranger School and the post-9/11 military setting make deprivation, leadership, duty, and example more important than ego display.
chapters.coreMove: Let uncommon performance steady the room instead of using it to stand above the room.
chapters.commonMisread: Be better than elite people so you can look superior.

chapters.title: The Empowerment of Failure
chapters.sourcePressure: Delta Force failure and pull-up record attempts teach that failure gains power only through honest review, correction, and renewed respect for the standard.
chapters.coreMove: Strip failure of ego protection until it becomes a correction sheet.

chapters.title: What If?
chapters.sourcePressure: Addison's disease, forced stillness, stretching-based recovery, retirement, brother reconciliation, and a closing question make the final discipline reflective rather than triumphant.
chapters.coreMove: Use stillness and repair to ask what possibility remains after proving is no longer the whole point.
chapters.commonMisread: The ending is a soft victory lap.
